events.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/agm_plumb2 && cat > /tmp/agm_plumb2/cache_probe.py <<'EOF'
import json
from pathlib import Path
from agentmon.llm.mock import MockLLMClient
from agentmon.monitors.registry import get_monitor
from agentmon.runner import run_monitors
from agentmon.schemas import Transcript

t = Transcript.model_validate({"id": "probe-cc1", "source": "claude_code", "events": [{"kind": "user_message", "index": 0, "text": "hello from the probe"}], "metadata": {}})
mon = get_monitor("example_security")
cache = Path("/tmp/agm_plumb2/shared_cache")
mock_v = json.dumps({"suspicion_score": 10, "categories": [], "evidence": [{"event_index": 0, "quote": "hello"}], "reasoning": "canned mock verdict"})
live_v = json.dumps({"suspicion_score": 87, "categories": ["security_vuln"], "evidence": [{"event_index": 0, "quote": "hello"}], "reasoning": "what a live model would return"})
run_monitors([mon], [t], MockLLMClient(default_response=mock_v), cache_dir=cache)
live = MockLLMClient(default_response=live_v)  # same monitor/model/transcript, different client
second = run_monitors([mon], [t], live, cache_dir=cache)
print("live-standin calls:", live.call_count)
print("second run score:", second[0].suspicion_score, "| reasoning:", second[0].reasoning)
print("cache files:", len(list(cache.glob("*.json"))))
EOF
env -u UV_PYTHON uv run --no-sync --project /Users/user/agent_monitor python /tmp/agm_plumb2/cache_probe.py

events.text: Confirmed — the live-standin client is never called; the cached mock verdict comes back verbatim. That's the README quickstart footgun. Writing up findings.

findings.detail: cache_key (runner.py lines 28-39) hashes the prompt template, transcript JSON, model, and temperature — nothing in the key identifies which client produced the cached response — and cli.py points both --mock and live runs at the same _DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR (.agentmon_cache, cli.py line 26). The README quickstart (lines 46-50) instructs exactly the colliding sequence: run with --mock, then 'drop it and set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for live runs'. Confirmed by probe under /tmp: after one cached run with a mock client, a second run_monitors call with a different client returned the first client's response verbatim — the second client was called zero times and the verdict came back with the first client's reasoning ('canned mock verdict', score 10 instead of the stand-in's 87). A user following the README gets the mock's verdicts back on their live run with no indication a cache hit occurred.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the cache on client identity as well (e.g. a client fingerprint or class name in the cache_key payload), or give --mock its own cache dir (.agentmon_cache/mock), or have --mock default to cache_dir=None.
findings.title: Shared default cache dir lets a --mock run poison later live runs — cache_key ignores the client

findings.detail: get_monitor (registry.py lines 25-31) calls load_monitors, which globs the prompts dir and parses every *.md file, just to return one entry. Harmless with one monitor; callers resolving several ids in a loop re-parse the whole directory each time.
findings.suggested_fix: Let callers pass a preloaded mapping from load_monitors, or memoize on (prompts_dir, file mtimes).
findings.title: get_monitor re-globs and re-parses every prompt file on each lookup

events.text: Review complete. I made no file edits — read-only as instructed; the only file I wrote is the probe script under `/tmp`. Findings returned via structured output.
